catalog_locator: p. 4, section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)'; supporting forms p. 2 and p. 3
catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) The stress is predictable and usually on the penultimate syllable. [p. 4] ... When the phoneme /a/ is word final or in weak (unstressed) syllables it is manifested phonetically as the raised form [ʌ]. [p. 3] ... valam ['Balam] 'cry' / veku ['Beku] 'stone' / vinae ['Binae] 'climb' [p. 2] ... iagu ['yagu] 'my' [p. 3]

new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) The stress is predictable and usually on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Canavan, Alan (data checked by Fred Madden, September 1992; updated June 1999). Organised Phonology Data: Bwanabwana (Tubetube) Language [TTE], Samarai District, Milne Bay Province. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG Branch manuscript, 6 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives item 42253, 'Tubetube Organised Phonology Data', draft posted as is; printed 7 Sep 2004).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (6 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'OPD', Subject 'Tubetube (Bwanabwana)', Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-09-06). Page 4, under the bold heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', reads exactly 'The stress is predictable and usually on the penultimate syllable.' — confirmed both in the extracted text (lines 118-119 of) and on a rendered image of p.4. Identity: p.1 header 'Organised Phonology Data / Bwanabwana (Tubetube) Language [TTE] / Samarai District – Milne Bay Province / Oceanic; Papuan Tip Cluster; Nuclear Papuan Tip; Suau Network', villages incl. Tubetube, Wale, Kwalaiwa islands = Glottolog bwan1241 [tte] (Suauic) with its two dialects Kwalaiwa and Wale;…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable of the word as a rule ('usually'); the same document says /a/ has a raised allophone word-finally and in weak (unstressed) syllables, consistent with final syllables being unstressed, and treats surface CVC (final m/n) words as underlying CV.CV.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'usually'; no exceptions listed. Note that Lithgow 1976:475 (Papuan-Tip-wide) says stress in the cluster's languages shifts one syllable rightward when a plural or object suffix is added, which is compatible with penultimate stress computed on the suffixed word.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word; single-word citation forms in an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet. Names the language as Bwanabwana (Tubetube) [TTE]; data from 15 years of SIL work, checked by a native speaker.
new_statements.identity_note: The source names the language 'Bwanabwana (Tubetube) Language [TTE]' = bwan1241 exactly (Glottolog dialects Kwalaiwa kwal1256 and Wale wale1245 are not distinguished in the OPD; villages listed include Tubetube, Wale and Kwalaiwa islands). The earlier scan classification no source found is superseded: the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (archive item 42253) exists and states stress.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.note: §84 STRESS (p.475) is a Papuan-Tip-wide note: stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima (probably Nimowa, Sud-Est); elsewhere 'predictable within certain word-classes' with stress shifting one syllable rightward under suffixation; nothing specific to Tubetube.
